label: L=3 sequences: final copy step (outputting 3rd original token)
explanation: Length-specific position unit. Fires almost only in length-3 sequences during the copy phase (99% of activation mass is at L=3), and mainly at the last copy step t=5, where it outputs original token 2 and the input is the fed-back token 1 (two steps after <DEL>). This step holds ~90% of the mass and nearly all top activations. It also fires weakly at the first L=3 copy output step (t=4, recall_idx=1), on about 30% of sequences and mostly in the bottom activation quartiles. Very rarely it fires at recall_idx 2 in L=4 sequences. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or for L>=5. Magnitude is somewhat larger when the original tokens contain no digits (n_digits=0 holds 67% of the mass). The few false positives at L=3,t=5 tend to have first token h or i. Token identity otherwise has little effect.

issues: The n_digits claim is overstated. On test, n_digits==0 sequences make up about 66% of the predicted L=3,t=5 steps (1721 of 2604), so their 67% share of mass mostly reflects how common they are. Mass per step is only about 10% higher (0.614/1721 vs 0.285/883), and precision is about the same (0.95 vs 0.92).

The missed activations (10% of mass, 901 steps on test) are a known, structural class: L=3, t=4, recall_idx=1. They sit mainly in the lowest activation quartile, and no simple token condition picks them out. Adding them, even restricted to n_digits==0, lowers F1 to 0.77 or below.

The other claims check out on test. The unit never fires in the original or delimiter phases (precision 0 for phase<2). It is essentially silent at L>=5. L=4, recall_idx=2 fires rarely (mass 0.006). L=3,t=4 has precision about 0.31. False positives with first token h or i: precision 0.625, compared with 0.94 overall.
